subject.title: fix(codex): clean final/yield turn close writes a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout

question: Should a successful Codex `final:true` message or `sessions_yield` keep the turn alive for natural completion—up to a fixed 10-second fallback window and with post-final output retained—or should OpenClaw preserve immediate hard-stop semantics?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent and real-behavior-proven, but it selects user-visible terminal timing, post-final output, and inbound-message policy that current behavior does not settle.

options.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
options.body: Keep the proposed natural `turn/completed` path, a fixed 10-second fallback interrupt, and immediate fallback when new inbound work arrives.

options.title: Preserve immediate hard stop
options.body: Retain the existing interrupt-on-terminal-delivery semantics and accept Codex’s current rollout marker behavior until an upstream graceful-stop protocol exists.

options.title: Choose a narrower variant
options.body: Adopt natural completion but specify a different deadline or a different rule for post-final output before the branch is rebased.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed natural `turn/completed` path, a fixed 10-second fallback interrupt, and immediate fallback when new inbound work arrives.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged source-reply finalization work establishes the nearest current-main terminal/finality contract affected by this choice.
